problem: The lead says inference, 'deciding whether one sentence follows from another', 'becomes a finite computation on those forms'. In full first-order logic entailment is only semidecidable: a proof search may run forever, and no terminating procedure decides it in general. As written, a student will believe FOL inference always halts.
fix: Say that inference becomes symbol manipulation on logical forms instead of on English, and add that in full first-order logic the check may not terminate; practical systems (databases, description logics) restrict the language so that it does. Example: 'Inference is now a search over those forms rather than over English. In full FOL that search is not guaranteed to halt, which is why deployed systems use restricted languages where it does.'

problem: The display line begins with the bare token '[formula]', a leftover placeholder that is not part of the formula and will confuse a reader about what the expression is.
fix: Delete it and write the display as: ∀x(Student(x) → ∃y(Book(y) ∧ Reads(x, y)))

problem: 'Gita sold the car to Ravi' and 'Ravi bought the car from Gita' are not logically equivalent as formulas: Sell(Gita, car, Ravi) and Buy(Ravi, car, Gita) are different predicates, and making them equivalent needs meaning postulates. The sentence as written implies logic alone delivers the equivalence.
fix: Say the MR should map both to the same predicate with the same argument order (a single Sell/Transfer predicate, arguments in the same slots), possibly using meaning postulates that link buy and sell; the equivalence comes from that shared form, not from the connectives.

problem: The representation splits the verb's own arguments into separate predicates (Reader(e, Meera), Object(e, book1)). That is the neo-Davidsonian style; Davidson's original proposal keeps the verb's arguments inside the main predicate, Read(e, Meera, book1), and adds only modifiers like Place(e, library) as conjunctions.
fix: Note the distinction: Davidson's original form is ∃e(Read(e, Meera, book1) ∧ Place(e, library) ∧ Time(e, Monday)); the fully separated Reader/Object version is the neo-Davidsonian variant. Both give the point that adding 'slowly' only adds a conjunct.

where: Section 2 and Exam traps, free variables
problem: Saying a formula with a free variable 'has no truth value' is loose. Truth is defined relative to a model plus an assignment of values to the free variables; the formula lacks a truth value only when no assignment is given.
fix: Say: a formula with a free variable is not a sentence, so it is true or false only once each free variable is given a value by a variable assignment; without an assignment it has no truth value.
